usage: This is the standard, everyday greeting used from waking up until around noon. It is universally understood across the Levant and is appropriate for all levels of formality, from close friends to strangers. The phrase itself does not change based on the gender or number of people being addressed.

variants.label: casual
variants.note: A shortened, affectionate version used primarily with close friends and family.

variants.label: Lebanese / urban
variants.note: Extremely common in Lebanon and some urban areas of Syria due to French influence.

variants.label: enthusiastic
variants.note: Used to show pleasant surprise or extra warmth when greeting someone.

examples.arabic: صَبَاح الخَيْر يَا شَبَاب، كِيفْكُم اليَوْم؟
examples.transliteration: saba7 el khayr ya shabab, kifkom el yom?
examples.english: Good morning guys, how are you today?

examples.arabic: صَبَاح الخَيْر، فِيِّي أُطْلُب قَهْوَة لَوْ سَمَحْت؟
examples.transliteration: saba7 el khayr, fiyyi otlob ahwe law sama7t?
examples.english: Good morning, can I order a coffee please?

examples.arabic: صَبَاح الخَيْر يَا إِمِّي، شُو طَابْخَة اليَوْم؟
examples.transliteration: saba7 el khayr ya emmi, shu tabkha el yom?
examples.english: Good morning mom, what are you cooking today?
